title: How a Business Works
outcome: Map business functions; distinguish revenue, profit and cash; complete the baseline assessment.
evidence: Three checked responses + one concise management decision
case:
HUL provides the real-company lens for this consumer-goods case.

A fictional Bengaluru distributor, Namma FMCG, supplies household products to 40 neighbourhood shops. It has just completed a festival promotion and the sales team celebrates a strong month. The owner sees the sales report and asks the finance associate to approve an INR 80,000 delivery-van deposit by 16:00. Meanwhile, the warehouse needs cash for next week's replenishment. Retailers bought some stock on credit, and supplier payments include settlement of earlier purchases. The operations manager believes a profitable month automatically means enough money is available.

The credit controller expects further collections next week but has no confirmed promise today. You are not allowed to assume those collections will happen early. The owner wants a decision now, not a full annual financial statement. Work with the mini-ledger, distinguish earned profit from actual cash and protect the agreed minimum balance. The scenario is a teaching simulation; it is not an allegation about HUL or any real distributor.
concept: Revenue records earned services; receipts record cash collected. Profit is revenue less recognised expenses. Closing cash follows actual receipts and payments. A process handoff needs an owner, evidence and a control.
example: A separate job earns INR 8,000 on credit and incurs INR 3,000 paid costs. Profit is INR 5,000 but its immediate cash movement is negative INR 3,000.
task: 12 minutes: calculate profit, closing bank and cash available above reserve; then approve, defer or seek financing for the van deposit.
squad: Cash-room showdown: work in a four-person squad and rotate the decision-maker. Win by separating profit from cash and giving a revised decision that still respects the reserve.

title: Professional Identity and Teamwork
outcome: Develop professional introductions, assign squad roles and establish accountability and work standards.
evidence: Three checked responses + one concise management decision
case:
Infosys provides the real-company lens for this service-operations case.

You are part of a fictional service-delivery pod called Vayentra Digital. It must send a client onboarding pack at 18:00. The pack has four components and each requires a named owner. One experienced spreadsheet user wants to handle everything, while two quieter associates want a meaningful task. A second laptop is unavailable until 17:30. The manager will only accept a pack if a different person has checked the customer references and the commercial totals. The team has 45 minutes before the review slot begins.

The staffing table gives available minutes rather than permission to overload the fastest person. A coordinator cannot simply put five names against one output and call it teamwork. The pack may be assembled by one person, but its components must have traceable ownership and a fallback if someone drops out. This activity asks for a workable allocation, not a detailed project plan or a long personal biography. The service pod and its people are fictional.
concept: Accountability means one owner accepts a deliverable and confirms acceptance criteria. A reviewer checks work but does not erase ownership. Workload fairness is judged by attributable contributions, not speaking time.
example: A useful commitment reads: I own receipt matching, will submit the match log at 17:00, and will escalate missing reference numbers by 15:00.
task: 10 minutes: allocate three critical outputs, assign a backup/reviewer, and write one escalation rule.
squad: The missing teammate: work in a four-person squad and rotate the decision-maker. Win with one accountable owner per output, a realistic backup and no self-approval.

title: Workplace Communication
outcome: Write clarification emails, progress updates and professional escalation messages.
evidence: Three checked responses + one concise management decision
case:
Infosys provides the real-company lens for this service-operations case.

A fictional analytics support pod prepares a daily account briefing for its service manager. At 11:00 the manager asks: Send me our three best customers before the 16:00 credit review. The exported billing file is complete, but the collections feed contains missing dates and disputed amounts. A senior colleague suggests ranking customers by billed revenue because it is quick and easy to explain. The customer-success lead disagrees: the report will influence credit limits, so payment behaviour matters.

You have ten minutes to send a useful clarification without delaying all work. The manager does not want a long essay or a promise that cannot be met. A high-value customer is not automatically a low-risk debtor, and missing information is not a zero balance. Use the supplied data to describe what can be delivered now, identify one specific data gap, and propose a time for the next update. The customers and credit policies in this case are invented for classroom practice.
concept: A useful message states the decision, available evidence, missing information, proposed assumption and next update. Concision must not remove a material limitation. Never silently choose a metric that changes the decision.
example: Example subject: September debtor review - collection data needed by 14:00. First line: I can rank billed revenue now; I need payment dates to assess credit reliability.
task: 10 minutes: identify the misleading ranking, request the missing evidence and write one email of no more than 70 words.
squad: The impatient CFO: work in a four-person squad and rotate the decision-maker. Win by being brief without treating unknown payment history as good payment history.

title: Meetings and Reporting
outcome: Run a structured meeting; document decisions, owners, deadlines and approval requirements.
evidence: Three checked responses + one concise management decision
case:
Maruti Suzuki provides the real-company lens for this automotive-operations case.

A fictional regional dealership group is organising a weekend display event. Twelve demonstration vehicles are expected at the venue by Friday 17:00, but the logistics partner now forecasts Saturday morning. The sales lead has already invited prospective customers and wants to announce that the event will run exactly as planned. A substitute carrier can deliver on Friday for an additional INR 18,000. The operations lead has authority to approve only INR 10,000. The regional manager is available for a five-minute decision call at 15:00.

The problem is not solved by recording minutes after the deadline passes. The meeting needs to isolate the actual decision, route it to the correct approver and stop an unauthorised guarantee. A partial delivery is another option, but its effect on the customer experience must be made explicit. Your output is a three-line action record that someone could execute immediately. The dealership, event, authority limits and carrier offers are fictional, not Maruti Suzuki operating records.
concept: Minutes capture decisions and unresolved decisions, not a transcript. Escalation moves a decision to the person with authority before the risk becomes irreversible. An option is not approved merely because a squad likes it.
example: Action record: Operations lead to confirm substitute availability by 14:30; manager to approve or reject INR 4,000 at 15:00; client lead to communicate the approved plan by 15:30.
task: 12 minutes: record three decisions/actions with an owner and deadline, then state what the client can be told now.
squad: Five-minute war room: work in a four-person squad and rotate the decision-maker. Win by escalating in time and recording proposed actions separately from approved commitments.

title: Accounting Transactions
outcome: Interpret source documents; classify transactions and prepare journal entries.
evidence: Three checked responses + one concise management decision
case:
Titan provides the real-company lens for this consumer-retail case.

A fictional jewellery-and-accessories showroom uses a daily transaction desk to keep sales, advances and collections separate. Near closing time, a new associate receives three documents: a supplier invoice, a bank receipt against an old customer balance and an advance for a custom order not yet delivered. The sales dashboard has already counted all incoming money as today's revenue. The showroom manager wants the ledger corrected before the daily performance summary is sent.

The associate must follow the economic event, not simply copy the bank narration. The supplier invoice creates an obligation; collection of an old invoice clears a receivable; a customer advance is not earned revenue in this simplified exercise. Ignore GST and inventory expense recognition here so that the task focuses on three entries. The amounts are deliberately small enough to work manually in a few minutes. This fictional showroom is not a Titan store and the records are not Titan transactions.
concept: Debits increase assets and expenses; credits increase liabilities, equity and revenue. Collection of an existing receivable does not create revenue again. A refundable advance is a liability until the service is earned.
example: A client pays an INR 8,000 existing invoice: debit Bank 8,000, credit Trade receivables 8,000. Revenue was recognised when the service was earned.
task: 12 minutes: write the debit and credit for exactly three documents. State which receipt must not become current revenue.
squad: Ledger detective: work in a four-person squad and rotate the decision-maker. Win by balancing each entry and linking the classification to delivery or earlier recognition.

title: Excel and Data Cleaning
outcome: Preserve raw data; handle duplicates and missing values; apply formulas and validation checks.
evidence: Three checked responses + one concise management decision
case:
HUL provides the real-company lens for this consumer-goods case.

A fictional FMCG distributor combines two route files before planning tomorrow's replenishment. One spreadsheet was copied from a sales email and another exported from the warehouse system. Customer codes differ in spacing and letter case; one invoice has been repeated; and a numeric-looking amount is stored as text. The raw total looks plausible, so the route planner wants to use it immediately to allocate stock to busy stores.

A duplicate may cause excess replenishment, while careless deletion could remove a genuine repeat order. The approved duplicate key is the invoice ID, not the customer name or amount. Normalising text helps comparison but does not authorise inventing a missing invoice. Preserve the original extract, note the changes and produce only the corrected invoice count and total. This dataset is invented for training and does not describe the controls of HUL or any actual distribution partner.
concept: Preserve Raw, transform into Clean, and document Exceptions. Duplicate detection needs a business key and evidence. An error should be visible; replacing unknown amounts with zero creates misleading certainty.
example: For an Excel table named Clean, =SUMIFS(Clean[Amount],Clean[Customer],A2) totals an approved customer. =COUNTIF(Raw[ID],[@ID]) flags repeated IDs; it does not decide which row is valid.
task: 12 minutes: identify the duplicate, calculate the cleaned invoice count and sales total, and record one cleaning rule.
squad: Data-cleaning escape room: work in a four-person squad and rotate the decision-maker. Win by fixing the duplicate without deleting a valid repeated purchase.

case:
Infosys provides the real-company lens for this service-operations case.

title: Commercial Decision Making
outcome: Compare pricing and discount scenarios; calculate contribution, break-even and capacity effects.
evidence: Three checked responses + one concise management decision
case:
Titan provides the real-company lens for this consumer-retail case.

A fictional accessories retailer is choosing a weekend offer for a watch line. The store manager wants a 15% price reduction to match a competitor. The finance associate argues that the same discount would consume much of the contribution per watch. A lighter discount might protect profit, but its effect on demand is unknown. The marketing team has produced three possible sales-volume forecasts, none of which has been validated by a controlled test.

Work from unit contribution rather than gross sales alone. The exercise assumes that variable cost per watch stays constant over the proposed volumes and that the offer has a fixed event cost. Do not treat the highest forecast as a certainty. You only need to compare the current price with the 15% discount and calculate the break-even volume under the discounted offer. The products, prices and forecast are fictional and are not Titan pricing, margin or demand data.
concept: Contribution per unit = net price minus variable cost. Break-even units = fixed costs / unit contribution, rounded up for whole units. Capacity limits can make a discount unable to improve profit.
example: At net price 5,000 and variable cost 2,000, contribution is 3,000; fixed cost 60,000 requires 20 units to break even.
task: 12 minutes: calculate current contribution, discounted contribution and discounted break-even units; give a conditional recommendation.
squad: The pricing boardroom: work in a four-person squad and rotate the decision-maker. Win with a conditional decision that recognises both contribution and unsold-stock risk.

title: Resume and Portfolio Development
outcome: Translate assessed work into credible achievements and assemble an evidence-linked portfolio.

case:
Infosys provides the real-company lens for this service-operations case.

A fictional applicant for a junior finance-operations role has completed a classroom reconciliation project. Their first résumé says “Worked at Infosys and transformed finance with AI.” In reality, the student used an Infosys-inspired classroom case, reviewed 40 fictional transaction rows, found four mismatches and prepared a reconciliation note. A peer suggests keeping the inflated wording because recruiters may not open the portfolio. The interview panel, however, plans to ask the student to explain one specific decision.

The useful asset is the work evidence, not an invented employer relationship. Turn the activity into a truthful achievement that states the simulated setting, the task and a defensible result. Do not claim percentage improvement without a before-and-after measure. The exercise is not affiliated with Infosys, and completing it is not employment, an internship or an endorsement. Your output should fit in a résumé and withstand a follow-up question in an interview.
concept: A credible achievement names the task, method, scale, result and context. Simulation work is valuable when described honestly. Different roles need different evidence selections, not inflated titles.
example: Better: Built a simulated four-account ageing model, reconciled INR 100,000 outstanding and corrected a due-date classification error; workbook and test log available.
task: 10 minutes: choose two verifiable facts, identify one misleading claim and write a résumé bullet of at most 35 words.
squad: The recruiter cross-examination: work in a four-person squad and rotate the decision-maker. Win when every claim can be backed by a file or explained from your own work.

title: Hiring Simulation and Exit Assessment
outcome: Complete an independent practical assessment and demonstrate reasoning in a structured interview.
evidence: Three checked responses + one concise management decision
case:
Infosys provides the real-company lens for this service-operations case.

A fictional recruiter gives a commerce graduate a short practical test. A services team earned INR 100,000, incurred INR 70,000 of recognised expenses, received INR 40,000 from customers and paid INR 50,000 in cash. Opening bank was INR 20,000. The candidate must explain whether a profitable period automatically supports an immediate INR 25,000 payment. The interviewer is more interested in the candidate's reasoning than in a polished slide deck.

Treat this as an independent mini-test: no AI or peer help during the 12-minute work stage. Show the three requested amounts and state one limitation. After the independent stage, the squad can role-play the interview and an AI tool can challenge the explanation using the same fictional facts. Do not upload an unseen faculty assessment or reuse these familiar questions as proof of independent exit competence. This practice is not an Infosys hiring test or a hiring endorsement.
concept: A practical interview tests execution and reasoning under clear constraints. Ask essential clarification questions, show workings and label uncertainty. Strong candidates explain limitations without pretending to know.
example: Interview structure: situation, your task, action, result and verification. State which part was yours and what the reviewer changed.
task: 12 minutes, independently and without AI: calculate profit, closing bank and payment shortfall; explain the decision in 35 words.
squad: The interview hot seat: work in a four-person squad and rotate the decision-maker. Win by explaining the calculation without treating an AI-assisted rehearsal as an independent assessment.

title: Corporate Presentation Preparation
outcome: Rehearse the business demonstration, defend recommendations and complete the evidence review.
evidence: Three checked responses + one concise management decision
case:
Titan provides the real-company lens for this consumer-retail case.

A fictional retail team tests a clearer billing handoff at one counter for one afternoon. The observed average wait falls from eight to six minutes in a sample of twenty customers before and twenty after the change. One student wants to claim “We cut waiting time by 25% across all Titan stores.” The pilot has no control group, the after-sample was quieter and the team has not measured whether the result lasts for a full week. The sponsor still needs a useful next-step recommendation.

Your job is to make the evidence persuasive without overstating it. The percentage change is calculable, but the scope and limitations are equally important. Prepare a three-part management story: the problem, the observed result and the proposed next test. Do not claim that the real company ran this pilot. A strong presentation can be honest about uncertainty and still make a clear request. The counter, samples and intervention are entirely fictional.
concept: A strong demonstration shows a decision, input, check, output and limitation. A tested artifact is more persuasive than feature lists. Every team member must own a defensible contribution.
example: A seven-minute structure: problem 1 minute; evidence 1; demonstration 3; recommendation 1; limitations and next step 1.
task: 10 minutes: calculate the observed wait reduction, identify one limitation and write a 45-word management pitch.
squad: The 60-second board pitch: work in a four-person squad and rotate the decision-maker. Win with a memorable presentation that distinguishes observation from proven organisation-wide impact.

title: Corporate Demo Day and Industry Passport
outcome: Present the project, answer reviewer questions and complete individual evidence verification.
evidence: Three checked responses + one concise management decision
case:
Titan provides the real-company lens for this consumer-retail case.

A fictional management panel is considering whether to expand a student-designed billing handoff pilot. The proposal needs INR 12,000 for training and rollout support. The team estimates INR 4,000 of monthly gross time-value benefit, with INR 1,000 of additional monthly support effort. Only one counter has been tested, and the cash saving is not yet demonstrated: staff time released may be used for better service rather than reduce payroll. The panel has three minutes to hear a recommendation and challenge its assumptions.

A credible defence must state the scope, show the arithmetic and distinguish estimated time value from actual cash savings. The simple payback calculation here is only a classroom estimate using net monthly benefit; it ignores taxes, financing and time value of money. Recommend an approval condition, a measurable next test and a stop rule. The fictional sponsor is not Titan, and neither the demo nor the resulting portfolio claims company endorsement or guaranteed employment.
concept: A credential reports demonstrated performance within its assessment scope. Team achievement does not replace individual competence. A reviewer can recommend an improvement without claiming that a person is employable in every role.
example: A sound passport entry: Bank reconciliation - independently demonstrated on timed case; adjusted balance and timing bridge correct; evidence ID EXIT-B-02; reviewer and date recorded.
task: 12 minutes: calculate net monthly benefit and simple estimated payback; give one approval condition and defend the proposal.
squad: The investment committee: work in a four-person squad and rotate the decision-maker. Win by defending assumptions honestly and changing the recommendation when the evidence changes.
